8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

```plantuml
@startuml

title arborparser Model

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}
class LevelPattern {
    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}
class ParserHelper {
    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}
class PatternBuilder {
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Operation Specifications
BaseNode::concatNode
Summary: Appends the textual representation of another BaseNode to this node's content without inserting extra separators.
Algorithm:
  1. Let textToAppend = node.title followed by node.content.
  2. Set this.content = this.content + textToAppend.
  3. Leave node unchanged.
Related Features: content, title
Related Classes: BaseNode
Input: node — the BaseNode whose text is to be appended.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: node is not null.
Post-condition: This node's content contains the previous content plus the other node's title/content in order; no separator is inserted.

LevelPattern::getRegex
Summary: Returns the compiled regular expression for this heading pattern.
Algorithm:
  1. If a cached Pattern exists, return it.
  2. Otherwise compile regexText using Pattern.compile.
  3. Cache and return the compiled Pattern.
Related Features: regexText
Related Classes: None
Input: none.
Output: Pattern object matching the configured heading form.
Pre-condition: regexText is non-null and a valid regular expression.
Post-condition: The returned Pattern contains the capturing group used for the numbering text.

```text
If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode into a TreeNode by copying the title, level sequence, level text, and content.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy levelSeq, levelText, title, and content from the ChainNode.
  3. Initialize children as an empty list and parent as null.
  4. Return the TreeNode.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: chainnode — the ChainNode to convert.
Output: TreeNode with the same data.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null.
Post-condition: The returned TreeNode is independent; later mutation of its children or content does not mutate the original ChainNode unless shared string references are used.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary: Attaches a ChainNode that has been judged to be an immediate valid next node to the correct place in the tree, and updates the mutable current branch so that it ends at the newly created TreeNode.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a TreeNode from the ChainNode using createTreeNode.
  2. Search currentBranch from the end to the beginning for the deepest ancestor whose levelSeq equals getPrefix(node.levelSeq).
  3. Attach the new TreeNode to that ancestor with addChild.
  4. Truncate currentBranch after that ancestor.
  5. Append the new TreeNode to currentBranch.
Related Features: createTreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy.getPrefix, TreeNode.addChild, currentBranch
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: node — the valid ChainNode to attach; currentBranch — mutable list of TreeNodes from root to current node.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: node is not null; currentBranch is not empty; the parent of node exists in currentBranch.
Post-condition: The node is attached under the correct ancestor, parent-child links are consistent, and currentBranch ends with the new TreeNode.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary: Checks whether all queued pending nodes form one uninterrupted sibling sequence: same level prefix and consecutive last level values.
Algorithm:
  1. If the queue has fewer than two nodes, return false.
  2. Let prefix = getPrefix(first.levelSeq).
  3. For each subsequent node, verify getPrefix(node.levelSeq) equals prefix and getLastLevel(node.levelSeq) equals getLastLevel(previous.levelSeq) + 1.
  4. Return true only if all checks succeed.
Related Features: TreeBuildingStrategy.getPrefix, TreeBuildingStrategy.getLastLevel
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: queue — Deque of pending ChainNodes.
Output: boolean; true if all nodes form a consecutive sibling sequence.
Pre-condition: queue is not null.
Post-condition: The queue is not modified.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary: Attaches a ChainNode into the tree under the nearest suitable ancestor in currentBranch, but does not update the branch list. The newly created TreeNode is made available through currentNodeRef.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a TreeNode from node using createTreeNode.
  2. Find the deepest TreeNode in currentBranch whose levelSeq equals getPrefix(node.levelSeq).
  3. Call parent.addChild(newNode).
  4. Set currentNodeRef to newNode.
Related Features: createTreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy.getPrefix, TreeNode.addChild
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: node — the ChainNode to attach; currentBranch — list of TreeNodes on the current valid branch; currentNodeRef — mutable holder for the created TreeNode.
Output: void; currentNodeRef is updated.
Pre-condition: node is not null; a suitable parent for node exists in currentBranch.
Post-condition: The tree contains the new TreeNode under the correct parent; currentBranch is unchanged; currentNodeRef references the new node.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a tree from a parsed chain using the tolerant auto-prune strategy. It maintains one latest valid branch, uses a pending queue for non-immediate nodes, and either attaches pending sibling groups or merges pending nodes into content.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with an empty level sequence.
  2. If the first chain node is a root node, use it as the tree root and start from the next node; otherwise create a synthetic root and start from the first node.
  3. Let currentBranch = [root], pending = empty Deque, and current = root.
  4. For each remaining ChainNode cn:
     a. If cn is a root node, skip it.
     b. If pending is not empty and cn is the immediate valid next node of the current branch, merge all pending nodes into current.content in arrival order, clear pending, attach cn using addNodeAndUpdateBranch, and update current.
     c. If pending is empty and cn is immediate, attach cn using addNodeAndUpdateBranch and update current.
     d. Otherwise add cn to the end of pending.
     e. While pending has at least three nodes:
        i. If isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending) is true, attach all pending nodes using addNodeAndUpdateBranch in order, clear pending, and update current.
        ii. Otherwise remove the oldest pending node and merge it into current.content.
  5. After all input nodes have been processed, merge all remaining pending nodes into current.content in arrival order.
  6. Return root.
Related Features: isRoot, isImmNext, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings, addNodeAndUpdateBranch, BaseNode.concatNode, getPrefix
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: chain — List<ChainNode>; may contain a synthetic root ChainNode.
Output: TreeNode root of the built tree.
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: The returned tree has a root titled "ROOT" when no root chain node was supplied; valid headings are attached; invalid pending nodes are folded into content without extra separators.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary: Returns the concatenation of this node's content and all descendants' content in pre-order without extra separators.

  2. For each child in children, append child.getFullContent().

Related Classes: TreeNode

Output: String.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: The tree is not modified.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary: Appends a child to this node and maintains consistent parent-child links.
Algorithm:
  1. If child is null or child is this node, throw an exception.
  2. If child.parent is not null, remove child from its old parent's children list.
  3. Add child to this.children.
  4. Set child.parent = this.
Related Features: children, parent
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: child — TreeNode to add.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: child is not null and is not an ancestor of this node.
Post-condition: child is in this.children, child.parent == this, and the old parent no longer contains child.

TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary: Destructively merges all descendant content into this node's content in pre-order and detaches the children.
Algorithm:
  1. Recursively call mergeAllChildren on each child.
  2. Let sb = new StringBuilder(this.content).
  3. For each child, append child.content to sb.
  4. Set this.content = sb.toString().
  5. Clear this.children and set each former child's parent to null.
Related Features: content, children, parent, mergeAllChildren
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: none.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: This node has no children; its content equals the previous full subtree content in traversal order.

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary: Recursive helper that renders a TreeNode and its children as indented text.
Algorithm:
  1. Build the current line: if isRoot is false, prefix with "└── " when isLast is true, otherwise "├── ".
  2. Append node.title and a newline.
  3. Compute childPrefix: if isRoot is false, append "    " when isLast is true, otherwise "│   ".
  4. Recursively call exportTreeInternal for each child, passing isLast only for the last child.
Related Features: title, children
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: node — TreeNode; prefix — accumulated indentation string; isLast — whether this node is the last child; isRoot — whether this node is the root.
Output: String.
Pre-condition: node is not null.
Post-condition: No tree mutation occurs.

TreeExporter::exportChain
Summary: Exports a parsed chain as one deterministic line per ChainNode.
Algorithm:
  1. For each ChainNode, format its levelSeq as dot-separated integers; an empty sequence is rendered as an empty string.
  2. Append "LEVEL-" + levelSeqText + ": " + title + "\n".
  3. Return the concatenated string.
Related Features: title, levelSeq
Related Classes: ChainNode
Input: chain — List<ChainNode>.
Output: String.
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: The output is deterministic and contains one line per node.

TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary: Returns a deterministic human-readable text tree.
Algorithm:
  1. Call exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true).
  2. Return the resulting string.
Related Features: exportTreeInternal
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: tree — TreeNode root.
Output: String.
Pre-condition: tree is not null.
Post-condition: The output is deterministic and visually represents the hierarchy.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary: Writes the JSON representation of a tree to a file using stable four-space indentation.
Algorithm:
  1. Convert tree to a JSON-compatible map using nodeToDict.
  2. Serialize the map with toJson(obj, 0).
  3. Write the string to filePath as UTF-8, overwriting an existing file.
Related Features: nodeToDict, toJson
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: tree — TreeNode; filePath — Path of the output file.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: tree and filePath are non-null; filePath is writable.
Post-condition: The file exists and contains deterministic, pretty-printed JSON with four-space indentation.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary: Converts a TreeNode into a JSON-compatible map with the required field names.
Algorithm:
  1. Create an ordered map.
  2. Set "title" to node.title.
  3. Set "level_seq" to node.levelSeq.
  4. Set "level_text" to node.levelText.
  5. Set "content" to node.content.
  6. Set "children" to a list created by calling nodeToDict on each child in order.
  7. Return the map.
Related Features: title, levelSeq, levelText, content, children
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: node — TreeNode.
Output: Map<String, Object> suitable for JSON serialization.
Pre-condition: node is not null.
Post-condition: Child order is preserved.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses plain structured text into a list of ChainNodes, preserving ordinary text as content of the current section and always providing a synthetic root when needed.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a root ChainNode with levelSeq = [], title = "ROOT", levelText = "", content = "", patternPriority = -1.
  2. Add the root to the chain and set current = root.
  3. Split text into lines while preserving original line separators.
  4. For each line:
     a. Call detectLevel(line).
     b. If the result is non-null, append it to the chain and set current to it.
     c. Otherwise append the raw line, including its original line terminator, to current.content.
  5. Return the chain.
Related Features: detectLevel, createChainNode
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern
Input: text — the raw structured document text.
Output: List<ChainNode>; the first element is the synthetic ROOT node when the document has leading/unmatched content or no headings.
Pre-condition: text is not null.
Post-condition: Leading unmatched text belongs to ROOT; text after a heading belongs to that heading until the next heading; no heading text is silently discarded.

ChainParser::detectLevel

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses plain structured text into a list of ChainNodes, preserving ordinary text as content of the current section and always providing a synthetic root when needed.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a root ChainNode with levelSeq = [], title = "ROOT", levelText = "", content = "", patternPriority = -1.
  2. Add the root to the chain and set current = root.
  3. Split text into lines while preserving original line separators.
  4. For each line:
     a. Call detectLevel(line).
     b. If the result is non-null, append it to the chain and set current to it.
     c. Otherwise append the raw line, including its original line terminator, to current.content.
  5. Return the chain.
Related Features: detectLevel, createChainNode
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern
Input: text — the raw structured document text.
Output: List<ChainNode>; the first element is the synthetic ROOT node when the document has leading/unmatched content or no headings.
Pre-condition: text is not null.
Post-condition: Leading unmatched text belongs to ROOT; text after a heading belongs to that heading until the next heading; no heading text is silently discarded.

ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Determines whether a single line is a heading by trying all configured LevelPattern objects in priority order.
Algorithm:
  1. For each pattern in patterns, in list order:
     a. Match the line against pattern.getRegex().
     b. If matched, extract the captured numbering text.
     c. Convert it to a level sequence using pattern.convertMatchedText.
     d. If conversion succeeds, create a ChainNode with that levelSeq, the raw line as title, empty content, the matched numbering as levelText, and the current pattern index as patternPriority.
     e. If conversion fails and the pattern requires conversion success, skip to the next pattern.
  2. If no pattern produces a valid level sequence, return null.
Related Features: patterns, createChainNode, LevelPattern.getRegex, LevelPattern.convertMatchedText
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern
Input: line — a single line of text, without a trailing newline.
Output: ChainNode if the line is a valid heading, otherwise null.
Pre-condition: line is not null.
Post-condition: No pattern or parser state is mutated; the first valid pattern determines the returned priority.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Creates a new ChainNode with the supplied parsed heading data.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a ChainNode.
  2. Set levelSeq, title, content, levelText, and patternPriority.
  3. If levelSeq is null, store an empty list.
  4. Return the new ChainNode.
Related Features: patterns
Related Classes: ChainNode, BaseNode
Input: levelSeq — List<Integer> level sequence; title — heading line/title; content — accumulated ordinary text; levelText — raw numbering text; patternPriority — priority order index of the matched pattern.

PatternBuilder::modify
Summary: Returns a new PatternBuilder with prefixRegex and minLevel changed, preserving all other settings.
Algorithm:
  1. Copy this builder using copySelf.
  2. Set copy.prefixRegex = newPrefixRegex.
  3. Set copy.minLevel = newMinLevel.
  4. Call copy.validate().
  5. Return the copy.
Related Features: copySelf, validate, prefixRegex, minLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input: newPrefixRegex — new prefix regular expression; newMinLevel — new minimum level value.
Output: PatternBuilder with modified fields.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is valid; newMinLevel is positive and not greater than maxLevel.
Post-condition: The original builder is unchanged.

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates the consistency of this PatternBuilder before building a LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
  1. Check that numberType is not null.
  2. Check that prefixRegex and suffixRegex are non-null and compile as valid regular expressions.
  3. Check that separator is non-null.
  4. Check that minLevel is positive and minLevel <= maxLevel.
  5. Throw an appropriate exception if any invariant is violated.
Related Features: numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator, minLevel, maxLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input: none.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: If valid, the builder remains usable; if invalid, an exception is thrown and the builder is not changed.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary: Creates an independent copy of this PatternBuilder.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new PatternBuilder.
  2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex.
  3. Return the copy.
Related Features: maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex
Related Classes: PatternBuilder

Output: PatternBuilder copy.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: Subsequent changes to the copy do not affect this builder.

```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

```plantuml
class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}
class LevelPattern {
    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}
class ParserHelper {
    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}
class PatternBuilder {
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
```

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::modify
Summary: Returns a new PatternBuilder with prefixRegex and minLevel changed, preserving all other settings.
Algorithm:
  1. Copy this builder using copySelf.
  2. Set copy.prefixRegex = newPrefixRegex.
  3. Set copy.minLevel = newMinLevel.
  4. Call copy.validate().
  5. Return the copy.
Related Features: copySelf, validate, prefixRegex, minLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input: newPrefixRegex — new prefix regular expression; newMinLevel — new minimum level value.
Output: PatternBuilder with modified fields.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is valid; newMinLevel is positive and not greater than maxLevel.
Post-condition: The original builder is unchanged.

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates the consistency of this PatternBuilder before building a LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
  1. Check that numberType is not null.
  2. Check that prefixRegex and suffixRegex are non-null and compile as valid regular expressions.
  3. Check that separator is non-null.
  4. Check that minLevel is positive and minLevel <= maxLevel.
  5. Throw an appropriate exception if any invariant is violated.
Related Features: numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator, minLevel, maxLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input: none.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: If valid, the builder remains usable; if invalid, an exception is thrown and the builder is not changed.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary: Creates an independent copy of this PatternBuilder.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new PatternBuilder.
  2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex.
  3. Return the copy.
Related Features: maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input: none.
Output: PatternBuilder copy.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: Subsequent changes to the copy do not affect this builder.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Checks whether childSeq is a direct structural child of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
  1. Return true if childSeq.size() == parentSeq.size() + 1 and childSeq's first parentSeq.size() elements equal parentSeq.
  2. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: None
Input: parentSeq — List<Integer>; childSeq — List<Integer>.
Output: boolean.
Pre-condition: Both sequences are non-null.
Post-condition: The input sequences are not modified.

StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a tree using strict rules. The chain must begin with a root node, and every following heading must be the immediate valid next heading relative to the current branch.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with an empty level sequence.
  2. If the first ChainNode is not a root node, reject the chain.
  3. Let root = createTreeNode(first root node) and currentBranch = [root].
  4. For each remaining ChainNode:
     a. Create a TreeNode.
     b. If the new node is not the immediate valid next node after currentBranch.last, reject the chain.
     c. Find the deepest ancestor in currentBranch whose levelSeq equals getPrefix(newNode.levelSeq).
     d. Attach new TreeNode to that ancestor.
     e. Truncate currentBranch after that ancestor and append the new TreeNode.
  5. Return root.
Related Features: createTreeNode, isRoot, isImmNext, getPrefix, TreeNode.addChild
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: chain — List<ChainNode>; must begin with a root node for strict construction.
Output: TreeNode root.
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: A strict tree is returned, or an exception is thrown if the chain cannot be strictly attached to the root.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode into a TreeNode for the strict strategy.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy levelSeq, levelText, title, and content from the ChainNode.
  3. Initialize children as empty and parent as null.
  4. Return the TreeNode.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: chainnode — ChainNode to convert.
Output: TreeNode.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null.
Post-condition: The returned TreeNode contains the same data.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Checks whether childSeq is a direct structural child of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
  1. Return true if childSeq.size() == parentSeq.size() + 1 and childSeq's first parentSeq.size() elements equal parentSeq.
  2. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: None
Input: parentSeq — List<Integer>; childSeq — List<Integer>.
Output: boolean.
Pre-condition: Both sequences are non-null.
Post-condition: The input sequences are not modified.

StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a tree using strict rules. The chain must begin with a root node, and every following heading must be the immediate valid next heading relative to the current branch.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with an empty level sequence.
  2. If the first ChainNode is not a root node, reject the chain.
  3. Let root = createTreeNode(first root node) and currentBranch = [root].
  4. For each remaining ChainNode:
     a. Create a TreeNode.
     b. If the new node is not the immediate valid next node after currentBranch.last, reject the chain.
     c. Find the deepest ancestor in currentBranch whose levelSeq equals getPrefix(newNode.levelSeq).
     d. Attach new TreeNode to that ancestor.
     e. Truncate currentBranch after that ancestor and append the new TreeNode.
  5. Return root.
Related Features: createTreeNode, isRoot, isImmNext, getPrefix, TreeNode.addChild
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input: chain — List<ChainNode>; must begin with a root node for strict construction.
Output: TreeNode root.
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: A strict tree is returned, or an exception is thrown if the chain cannot be strictly attached to the root.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode into a TreeNode for the strict strategy.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy levelSeq, levelText, title, and content from the ChainNode.
  3. Initialize children as empty and parent as null.
  4. Return the TreeNode.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode
Input: chainnode — ChainNode to convert.
Output: TreeNode.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null.
Post-condition: The returned TreeNode contains the same data.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

```java
   * Summary: Parses plain structured text into a list of ChainNodes, preserving ordinary text as content of the current section and always providing a synthetic ROOT node.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Create a root ChainNode by calling createChainNode([], "ROOT", "", "", -1).
```

    // Split the text into lines, preserving each line's original terminator.

    int length = text.length();
    for (int i = 0; i < length; i++)

      char c = text.charAt(i);
      if (c == '\n')
      {
        lines.add(text.substring(start, i + 1));

```java
   * Summary: Builds a strict tree. An empty chain produces a synthetic root
   * titled "ROOT"; otherwise the chain must begin with a root node, and every
   * following node must be an immediate valid next heading relative to the
   * current branch.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If chain is empty, create a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with an
   *      empty level sequence, empty levelText, empty content, an empty children
   *      list, and null parent; return it.
   *   2. If the first ChainNode is not a root node, reject the chain.
   *   3. Let root = createTreeNode(first root node) and currentBranch = [root].
   *   4. For each remaining ChainNode:
   *      a. Create a TreeNode from the ChainNode.
   *      b. If isImmNext(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, newNode.levelSeq) is false,
   *         reject the chain.
   *      c. Find the deepest ancestor in currentBranch whose levelSeq equals
   *         getPrefix(newNode.levelSeq).
   *      d. Attach the new TreeNode to that ancestor with TreeNode.addChild.
   *      e. Truncate currentBranch after that ancestor and append the new TreeNode.
   *   5. Return root.
   * Related Features: createTreeNode, isRoot, isImmNext, getPrefix
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
   * Input: chain — List<ChainNode>; if non-empty, the first node must be a root node.
   * Output: TreeNode root.
   * Pre-condition: chain is not null.
   * Post-condition: A strict tree is returned, or an exception is thrown if the
```

    if (!isRoot(chain.get(0)))

    TreeNode root = createTreeNode(chain.get(0));

    currentBranch.add(root);

    for (int i = 1; i < chain.size(); i++)

      // Every following node must be an immediate valid next heading.
      TreeNode lastNode = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
      if (!isImmNext(lastNode.getLevelSeq(), newNode.getLevelSeq()))

      EList<Integer> prefix = getPrefix(newNode.getLevelSeq());

   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Return true if childSeq.size() == parentSeq.size() + 1 and childSeq's first parentSeq.size() elements equal parentSeq.
   *   2. Otherwise return false.
   * Related Features: None.
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input: parentSeq — List<EIntegerObject>; childSeq — List<EIntegerObject>.
   * Output: boolean.
   * Pre-condition: Both sequences are non-null.
   * Post-condition: The input sequences are not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model parentSeqMany="true" childSeqMany="true"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isChild(final EList<Integer> parentSeq, final EList<Integer> childSeq)
  {
    if (childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1)
    {
      return false;
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < parentSeq.size(); i++)
    {
      if (!childSeq.get(i).equals(parentSeq.get(i)))
      {
        return false;
      }
    }

    return true;
  }

```java
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If chain is empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with an empty level sequence.
   *   2. If the first chain node is a root node, use it as the tree root and start from the next node; otherwise create a synthetic root titled "ROOT" with an empty level sequence and start from the first node.
```

```java
   * Summary: Builds a tree from a parsed chain using the tolerant auto-prune strategy. It maintains one latest valid branch, uses a pending queue for non-immediate nodes, and either attaches pending sibling groups or merges pending nodes into content.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If chain is empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with an empty level sequence.
   *   2. If the first chain node is a root node, use it as the tree root and start from the next node; otherwise create a synthetic root titled "ROOT" with an empty level sequence and start from the first node.
   *   3. Let currentBranch = [root], pending = empty Deque, and current = root.

   *      b. If pending is not empty and cn is the immediate valid next node of the current branch, merge all pending nodes into current.content in arrival order, clear pending, attach cn using addNodeAndUpdateBranch, and update current.
   *      c. If pending is empty and cn is immediate, attach cn using addNodeAndUpdateBranch and update current.
   *      d. Otherwise add cn to the end of pending.
   *      e. While pending has at least three nodes:
```

   * @generated NOT

    // 1. Empty chain -> synthetic ROOT with an empty level sequence.
    if (chain.isEmpty())
    {
      TreeNode root = ArborparserFactory.eINSTANCE.createTreeNode();
      root.setTitle("ROOT");
      return root;
    }

    // 2. Determine the tree root and the first node to process.
    TreeNode root;
    int startIndex;
    if (isRoot(chain.get(0)))
    {
      root = createTreeNode(chain.get(0));
      startIndex = 1;
    }
    else
    {
      root = ArborparserFactory.eINSTANCE.createTreeNode();
      root.setTitle("ROOT");
      startIndex = 0;
    }

    // 3. Initialize the current branch, the pending queue and the current node.
    EList<TreeNode> currentBranch = new BasicEList<TreeNode>();
    currentBranch.add(root);
    Deque<ChainNode> pending = new ArrayDeque<ChainNode>();
    TreeNode current = root;

    // 4. Process each remaining chain node.

      ChainNode cn = chain.get(i);

      // a. Skip root nodes.
      if (isRoot(cn))
      {
        continue;
      }

      boolean isImmediate = isImmNext(current.getLevelSeq(), cn.getLevelSeq());

      // b. Pending nodes exist and cn is the immediate valid next node.
      if (!pending.isEmpty() && isImmediate)
      {
        for (ChainNode p : pending)
        {
          current.concatNode(p);
        }
        pending.clear();
        addNodeAndUpdateBranch(cn, currentBranch);
        current = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
      }
      // c. No pending nodes and cn is immediate.
      else if (pending.isEmpty() && isImmediate)
      {
        addNodeAndUpdateBranch(cn, currentBranch);
        current = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
      }
      // d. Otherwise buffer cn in the pending queue.
      else
      {
        pending.addLast(cn);
      }

      // e. While pending holds at least three nodes.
      while (pending.size() >= 3)
      {
        if (isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending))
        {
          for (ChainNode p : pending)
          {
            addNodeAndUpdateBranch(p, currentBranch);
            current = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
          }
          pending.clear();
        }
        else
        {
          ChainNode oldest = pending.removeFirst();
          current.concatNode(oldest);
        }
      }
    }

    // 5. Merge all remaining pending nodes into current.content in arrival order.
    for (ChainNode p : pending)
    {
      current.concatNode(p);
    }
    pending.clear();

    // 6. Return the root.
    return root;
  }

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Checks whether all queued pending nodes form one uninterrupted sibling sequence: same level prefix and consecutive last level values.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If the queue has fewer than two nodes, return false.
   *   2. Let prefix = getPrefix(first.levelSeq).
   *   3. For each subsequent node, verify getPrefix(node.levelSeq) equals prefix and getLastLevel(node.levelSeq) equals getLastLevel(previous.levelSeq) + 1.
   *   4. Return true only if all checks succeed.
   * Related Features: TreeBuildingStrategy.getPrefix, TreeBuildingStrategy.getLastLevel
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
   * Input: queue — Deque of pending ChainNodes.
   * Output: boolean; true if all nodes form a consecutive sibling sequence.
   * Pre-condition: queue is not null.
   * Post-condition: The queue is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model queueDataType="edu.arborparser.Deque&lt;edu.arborparser.ChainNode&gt;"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
```java
  public void isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(final Deque<ChainNode> queue)
  {
    if (queue.size() < 2)
    {
      return false;
    }
    ChainNode previous = queue.peekFirst();
    EList<Integer> prefix = getPrefix(previous.getLevelSeq());
    boolean first = true;
    for (ChainNode node : queue)
    {
      if (first)
      {
        first = false;
        continue;
      }
      if (!getPrefix(node.getLevelSeq()).equals(prefix))
      {
        return false;
      }
      if (getLastLevel(node.getLevelSeq()) != getLastLevel(previous.getLevelSeq()) + 1)
      {
        return false;
      }
      previous = node;
    }
    return true;
  }
```

```java
      if (isRoot(cn))
      {
        continue;
      }

      boolean isImmediate = isImmNext(current.getLevelSeq(), cn.getLevelSeq());

      // b. Pending nodes exist and cn is the immediate valid next node.
      if (!pending.isEmpty() && isImmediate)
      {
        for (ChainNode p : pending)
        {
          current.concatNode(p);
        }
        pending.clear();
        addNodeAndUpdateBranch(cn, currentBranch);
        current = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
      }
      // c. No pending nodes and cn is immediate.
      else if (pending.isEmpty() && isImmediate)
      {
        addNodeAndUpdateBranch(cn, currentBranch);
        current = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
      }
      // d. Otherwise buffer cn in the pending queue.
      else
      {
        pending.addLast(cn);
      }

      // e. While pending holds at least three nodes.
      while (pending.size() >= 3)
      {
        if (isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending))
        {
          for (ChainNode p : pending)
          {
            addNodeAndUpdateBranch(p, currentBranch);
            current = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
          }
          pending.clear();
        }
        else
        {
          ChainNode oldest = pending.removeFirst();
          current.concatNode(oldest);
        }
      }
    }

    // 5. Merge all remaining pending nodes into current.content in arrival order.
    for (ChainNode p : pending)
    {
      current.concatNode(p);
    }
    pending.clear();

    // 6. Return the root.
    return root;
  }

   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeBuildingStrategy

   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(final Deque<ChainNode> queue)
  {
    if (queue.size() < 2)
    {
      return false;
    }
    ChainNode previous = queue.peekFirst();
    EList<Integer> prefix = getPrefix(previous.getLevelSeq());
    boolean first = true;
    for (ChainNode node : queue)
    {
      if (first)
      {
        first = false;
        continue;
      }
      if (!getPrefix(node.getLevelSeq()).equals(prefix))
      {
        return false;
      }
      if (getLastLevel(node.getLevelSeq()) != getLastLevel(previous.getLevelSeq()) + 1)

        return false;
      }
      previous = node;
    }
    return true;
  }
```

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Checks whether all queued pending nodes form one uninterrupted sibling sequence: same level prefix and consecutive last level values.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If the queue has fewer than two nodes, return false.
   *   2. Let prefix = getPrefix(first.levelSeq).
   *   3. For each subsequent node, verify getPrefix(node.levelSeq) equals prefix and getLastLevel(node.levelSeq) equals getLastLevel(previous.levelSeq) + 1.
   *   4. Return true only if all checks succeed.
   * Related Features: TreeBuildingStrategy.getPrefix, TreeBuildingStrategy.getLastLevel
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
   * Input: queue — Deque of pending ChainNodes.
   * Output: boolean; true if all nodes form a consecutive sibling sequence.
   * Pre-condition: queue is not null.
   * Post-condition: The queue is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model queueDataType="edu.arborparser.Deque&lt;edu.arborparser.ChainNode&gt;"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(final Deque<ChainNode> queue)
  {
    if (queue.size() < 2)
    {
      return false;
    }
    ChainNode previous = queue.peekFirst();
    EList<Integer> prefix = getPrefix(previous.getLevelSeq());
    boolean first = true;
    for (ChainNode node : queue)
    {
      if (first)
      {
        first = false;
        continue;
      }
      if (!getPrefix(node.getLevelSeq()).equals(prefix))
      {
        return false;
      }
      if (getLastLevel(node.getLevelSeq()) != getLastLevel(previous.getLevelSeq()) + 1)
      {
        return false;
      }
      previous = node;
    }
    return true;
  }

} // AutoPruneStrategy

  1.2 Locate these files in your project.
  1.3 Generate the class summarization.
2. Read the error messages carefully.
3. Do your best to fix the errors locally without introducing new types, fields, and methods.
4. You should not remove faulty methods to eliminate compilation errors.
5. Do not change parts without errors.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.
